mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal from accelerating GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sharp INDPRO drop, indicating the supply shock is not reliably negative for equities.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as an increase of > 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points in the month following the UNRATE trigger, indicating the labor market weakening is not negatively impacting consumer sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, defined as the 10-year Treasury yield falling below the 2-year yield, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens by > 50 basis points within 3 months of inverting, indicating the tightening signal was false and not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, as measured by the year-over-year change in the HOUST index, signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The NAHB Housing Market Index rises by > 5 points in the month following the HOUST drop, indicating homebuilder sentiment remains strong despite the drop in housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the ISM Manufacturing PMI, defined as an increase of > 5 points over the past 3 months, signals a strengthening manufacturing sector that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The ISM New Orders index falls by > 5 points in the month following the ISM trigger, indicating the manufacturing strength is not translating into new business activity.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in wage growth, defined as the year-over-year change in average hourly earnings rising by > 1 percentage point over the past 3 months, signals a tightening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: AHETPI YoY change rises > 1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: Real consumer spending (PCE) falls by > 0.5% in the quarter following the wage growth trigger, indicating the wage acceleration is not translating into higher consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the M2 money supply, defined as the year-over-year change in M2 falling by > 2 percentage points over the past 3 months, signals a tightening of monetary conditions that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: M2SL YoY change falls > 2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: The Fed cuts interest rates by > 50 basis points within 3 months of the M2 drop, indicating the monetary tightening was temporary and likely to be reversed.
